Some Interesting Insights from Q2FY27 Concall:

- Orders per day per store reached close to 1,200, the best level ever, with NOV per store up 9% sequentially and orders per day up 9.5% sequentially; capacity utilization increased close to 10% on orders per day per store, still leaving sufficient room for growth.

- Every quarter roughly 5–7% of the network is close to max utilization (~2,000–2,500 orders/day); store addition is a factor of growth and will continue as growth maxes out capacity in hyperlocal zip codes, with no near-term expectation to increase geographical coverage beyond 130+ cities.

- The core business returned to 20%+ growth, with management maintaining 18–20% YoY standalone guidance for the full year.  - Food Delivery

- The audience is far younger than core Swiggy, with 70–80% of users sub-30 years of age, many in final years of college or first-time jobbers who will form the consuming class 3–5 years out. - Toing

eMudhra's decision to exit its global website security certificate business following a cryptographic key generation failure raises some serious questions. 

Eight intermediate certificate authorities were left vulnerable because the generated keys were weaker than intended. The output wasn't reviewed after the ceremony, and the company attributed the failure to a script error and human oversight.

For a company built around digital trust and security, this is more than just a technical glitch. When your entire business revolves around trust, even one lapse in execution can have serious consequences. 

The bigger questions are around internal controls, quality assurance, risk management and management oversight.

Everyone is chasing AI stocks. But look at India's upcoming investment pipeline:

🔹 ₹5.27 lakh crore - Semiconductors

Impressive numbers. But as an investor, I look at three things:

1. Capital Committed - What's announced.
2. Capital Deployed - What actually gets spent.
3. Shareholder Returns - What generates profits, free cash flow and ROCE.

The market celebrates the first, anticipates the second and often forgets the third.

📍 NEW PROJECTS

APOLLO MICRO SYSTEMS: Group company IDL Explosives commissions a 9,000 MT bulk explosives silo unit near Asansol, West Bengal, to serve mining operations in the eastern and central coal belts.

JTEKT INDIA: Approves expansion of its constant velocity joint line at Jalisana, Gujarat, by 0.8 million units, taking capacity beyond the existing 1.2 million units; completion targeted for August 2028.

DIACABS: Plans a ₹25 Cr investment in a new CCV line at Vadodara to manufacture XLPE-insulated power cables up to 132 kV, with capacity expected by December 2027.

SANDUR MANGANESE: Wholly owned subsidiary leases 6.2 acres at Andhra Pradesh MedTech Zone for a proposed medical devices manufacturing facility; capex and project timelines are yet to be announced.

PATEL RETAIL: Finalises two new store locations at Ghoti in Nashik district and Mangaon/Mahad in Raigad district, expanding its Maharashtra retail footprint.

JUNIPER GREEN ENERGY: Commissions an additional 33 MW of wind capacity through its subsidiary, taking its project capacity to 467.35 MWp with approximately 201 MWh of battery storage.

📍 FUNDRAISING

OLA ELECTRIC: Confirms applications by specific investors for 2.39 Cr rights entitlements renounced by promoter group entities ANI Technologies and Indus Trust on the rights issue opening date.

GUJARAT INJECT KERALA: Board to consider issuing equity shares and/or warrants through preferential allotment on 26 October; issue size and pricing have not been disclosed.

📍 INCORPORATE / CORPORATE STRUCTURE

PFC: Wholly owned subsidiary PFCCL incorporates Northern Region Power Transmission SPV for grid compensation requirements; the SPV is to be transferred to the successful bidder under tariff-based competitive bidding.

AVANCE TECHNOLOGIES: Incorporates wholly owned subsidiary Avance Holding Private Limited to undertake investment activities in securities and other financial instruments.

SHYAM METALICS: NCLT Kolkata approves amalgamation of Shree Venkateshwara Electrocast into wholly owned subsidiary Shyam Sel and Power, consolidating the aluminium foil business.

NIDHI GRANITES: Jowela Exim becomes its subsidiary following the allotment of 16 lakh equity shares under a rights issue.

📍 CREDIT RATINGS

MPHASIS: SBTi validates its near-term and net-zero emissions targets, including a 66.01% reduction in absolute Scope 1 and 2 emissions by FY36 and net-zero emissions across its value chain by FY50.

📍 USFDA / REGULATORY

CORONA REMEDIES: Receives ANVISA Brazil GMP certification for its oral solid dosage and hormone manufacturing facilities at Bhayla, Ahmedabad, opening regulatory access to the Brazilian market.

JAYKAY ENTERPRISES: Wholly owned subsidiary receives CDSCO licence to manufacture Class C and D orthopaedic and spinal implants under the Neobone and Nubone brands.

KSH INTERNATIONAL: Receives PGCIL approval to manufacture and supply specified copper conductors for transformers and reactors up to the 765 kV class for POWERGRID projects.

📍 Q2 / BUSINESS UPDATE

SWASTIKA INFRA: Q2 net profit rises 80% YoY to ₹16 Cr, revenue grows 42% to ₹148 Cr and EBITDA increases 65% to ₹27 Cr; unexecuted order book stands at ₹1,420 Cr.

INFINITY INFOWAY: H1 FY27 net profit increases 79.4% YoY to ₹5.02 Cr, revenue rises 106.2% to ₹16.81 Cr and EBITDA grows 109.7% to ₹8.52 Cr.

PAISALO DIGITAL: Q2 net profit increases 27.4% YoY to ₹65.64 Cr, while total income rises 23.8% to ₹277.31 Cr.

INTERNATIONAL GEMMOLOGICAL INSTITUTE: Expects at least mid-20% growth in FY27, with natural diamond business growth at 8% in H1 and double-digit growth expected for the full year.

RAJRATAN GLOBAL WIRE: Q2 revenue rises 26% YoY to ₹370.83 Cr, EBITDA increases 14% to ₹45.79 Cr and PAT grows 17% to ₹24.14 Cr; plans to add 50,000 TPA capacity in Thailand within a year.

MAHINDRA LIFESPACE DEVELOPERS: Q2 consolidated net profit falls 65.9% YoY to ₹16.34 Cr despite revenue growth; reported profit includes a ₹26.94 Cr gain from the Ample Parks divestment and a ₹25 Cr cost-to-completion reversal in other income.

HAVELLS INDIA: Reports strong growth across product categories, supported by demand and price increases, while cable and Lloyd margins remain under pressure from raw material inflation and under-absorption.

YASH HIGHVOLTAGE: Says EBITDA margin performance is being supported by volume growth and product mix, with gross margins expected to improve through indigenous manufacturing.

📍 LAUNCHES

INTELLECT DESIGN ARENA: Deploys its eMACH.ai lending platform at Jameel Finance in Egypt, covering loan origination, loan management, collections and BNPL; implementation completed in 16 weeks.

AMAGI: NDTV adopts its AdFlow Orchestrator to optimise advertising on FAST and connected TV platforms, with automated ad-break restructuring aimed at improving monetisation.

QUICK HEAL, TAC INFOSEC, SATTRIX, NPST AND TECHD CYBER: Cybersecurity-related websites reportedly face worldwide takedowns amid an AI-related security threat; individual company-specific impacts were not detailed in the supplied update.

EMUDHRA: Says the reported issue was a one-off incident on a bad day and confirms that Ministry of IT officials visited the company.

📍 CLARIFICATION

GARWARE HI-TECH FILMS: Says its TPU line commissioning remains on track for Q3 FY27, with further capacity expansion intended to support future growth; reports encashment of a ₹25 lakh bank guarantee by MPCB over alleged consent-condition non-compliance, while stating that corrective compliance steps have been taken.

* Millworks will retain exclusive rights to the manufacturing processes it develops for engine castings, seals and key components.

EMUDHRA : EXITS GLOBAL SSL/TLS CERTIFICATE BUSINESS

• Board decided to voluntarily withdraw from the global SSL/TLS certificate business
• Global SSL/TLS is a small part of business, contributing about 1% of global revenue
• Affected CAs revoked within 14 hours of discovery; no end entity certificates issued from affected CA, infrastructure not compromised, no data breached
• Company cites rising data sovereignty and compliance complexity, cost, and large entities issuing SSL/TLS free of cost as reasons for lower business potential and RoI
• G1 RSA roots to serve customers until transition is complete; affected customers to get free certificate replacement from partners; remaining browser root program commitments including full root-cause report to be completed
• Core businesses unaffected - DSC, eSign and other signing services in India, enterprise PKI (emCA, CertiNext), emSigner and identity solutions (SecurePass, emAS) continue normally
Impact: Neutral (exit covers only ~1% of global revenue while sharpening focus on core enterprise solutions and trust services; no breach or infrastructure compromise stated)

Looking ahead, PC Jeweller plans to establish up to 100 large-format showrooms across Tier I, II and III cities over the next 12–18 months. PRE-MARKET RADAR | STOCKS IN ACTION TODAY

🟢 POSITIVE
Defence orders, healthcare M&A and festive demand drive sentiment. Q2 results from NBFCs and certification companies were healthy.

- Bharat Electronics (BEL): Receives ₹1,011 Cr orders since Oct 13, including ₹770 Cr defence contract for Army radar systems. Balance includes communication kits, sonar, jammers, upgrades, spares and services.

- Yash Highvoltage: H1 FY27 revenue rises 95% to ₹194.5 Cr; PAT rises 157% to ₹36.2 Cr; EBITDA rises 136%. Order book exceeds ₹760 Cr; ₹220 Cr greenfield plant commissioning underway.

- Indian Hotels (IHCL): Q2 FY27 PAT rises 23% YoY. Consolidated EBITDA reaches ₹788 Cr at 30.7% margin. FY27 hotel revenue growth guidance raised to 17–19%.

- Mahindra Finance (M&MFIN): Q2 PAT rises 55% to ₹882 Cr. Targets 16–18% AUM growth and 2.2–2.5% ROA. Housing finance merger planned for mid-2027.

- International Gemmological Institute (IGIL): Q2 FY27 PAT rises 43% to ~₹186 Cr. Certification revenue rises 32% to ~₹388 Cr; EBITDA rises 39% to ~₹245 Cr.

- SEAMEC: Secures $55 million vessel charter from promoter HAL Offshore for ONGC offshore work. Contract duration is 1,225 days. Related-party transaction is reportedly at arm's length; promoter holds 70.8%.

- Sagility (SAGILITY): US subsidiary to acquire 100% of Chirok Health for up to $32.4 million. Consideration includes $20 million upfront and $12.4 million milestone-linked payments.

- Maruti Suzuki (MARUTI): Festive retail sales rise 35% from Ganesh Chaturthi to Dussehra. SUV sales double; small-car sales rise 16%. Pending bookings reach 2.7 lakh units versus 2 lakh in October.

- Anand Rathi Share (ANANDRATHI): Q2 FY27 PAT rises 50% to ~₹42 Cr. Revenue rises 20% to ~₹273 Cr; MTF book stands at ~₹1,499 Cr.

- Sanofi India (SANOFI): Receives CDSCO marketing authorisation for Qfitlia, a haemophilia bleeding-prevention treatment for adults and adolescents aged 12+.

- Sterling & Wilson: Kenya tax demand reduced to ₹2.7 Cr from ₹26.5 Cr. Interest and penalty waived if payment occurs by December 25, 2026.

🔴 NEGATIVE
Governance and regulatory developments dominate. Yes Bank's target cut and Adani Green's grid constraints warrant attention.

- Yes Bank (YESBANK): Stock falls 21% over five days following the AT1 verdict. Nomura cuts its target price to ₹18.

- Adani Green Energy (ADANIGREEN): Grid availability reportedly fell below 80% during the quarter. Expansion delays forced production curtailment. Source: ScoutQuest; unverified.

- Nestlé India (NESTLEIND): FSSAI seeks scientific evidence supporting infant formula and nutrition-product marketing claims, including Lactogen and Nan Excella. Zydus Wellness is also under scrutiny.

- Indosolar (INDOSOLAR): Q2 EBITDA falls 79% YoY to ₹14.8 Cr; margin stands at 9.5%. Module sales decline to 98 MW. Merger with Waaree Energies proposed.

- Container Corporation (CONCOR): Faces ~₹5.9 Cr GST demand for FY19, including tax, interest and penalty. Company plans to appeal and expects no material impact.

- Unifinz Capital: Reports ₹7.7 Cr cyber fraud involving 346 unauthorised transactions from its disbursal account. Account frozen; cybercrime complaint filed.

- AMD Industries (AMDIND): CFO Sanjeev Kumar Singhal resigns effective October 21, citing personal reasons.

- Star Paper Mills (STARPAPER): Receives ~₹1.5 Cr GST demand for FY24, including interest and penalty. Appeal planned; no material impact expected.

⚪️ NEUTRAL / CORPORATE ACTIONS
Fundraises, buybacks and corporate developments dominate. Persistent Systems' QIP is the largest transaction.

- Persistent Systems (PERSISTENT): QIP opens with ₹5,550 floor price. Issue size up to $450 million (~₹4,265 Cr).

- L&T Finance (LTF): Allots 1.5 lakh secured NCDs worth ₹1,500 Cr at 7.9% coupon, maturing September 2029. Option for another 50,000 NCDs.

- Reliance Industries (RELIANCE): ICRA reaffirms AAA/Stable on NCDs and assigns AAA/Stable to ₹50,000 Cr bank facilities. ₹10,000 Cr commercial paper receives A1+ rating. Moody's says Jio's ₹30,213 Cr IPO will reduce RIL debt.

- Jubilant Pharmova (JUBLPHARMA): India Ratings assigns IND AA+/Stable to proposed ₹1,400 Cr NCDs.

- Eternal (ETERNAL): Q2 PAT rises 92% to ₹125 Cr; revenue rises 78%, but results miss estimates. Targets 3,500 stores by March 2027 and ~5,000 by March 2028. Stock closes down 2.5%.

- Gujarat Mineral Development Corporation (GMDCLTD): Presents ₹223.55 Cr dividend cheque to Gujarat Government. Total payout is ₹302.1 Cr, including FY26 final dividend of ₹9.50/share.

- Shivam Autotech: Rights issue resized to ~₹120 Cr, comprising 9.99 Cr shares at ₹12. Opens October 28; listing expected around November 25.

- Virtual Global Education: Board approves ₹42 Cr preferential warrant issue and subsidiary Shikshan School sale. CFO Gaurav Garg resigns; Krishan Bansal appointed CFO and Executive Director from October 21.

- Advanced Enzyme Technologies (ADVENZYMES): Buys back 57,000 shares at average ₹262.80, worth ~₹1.5 Cr. Cumulative buyback reaches 21.43 lakh shares.

- Man Infraconstruction (MANINFRA): Buys back 1.3 lakh shares at average ₹110.40, worth ~₹1.4 Cr. Cumulative buyback reaches 99.2 lakh shares.

- Uno Minda (UNOMINDA): Targets ~₹40,000 Cr revenue by FY30 versus ₹19,700 Cr in FY26. Growth drivers include EV drives, seating, sunroofs and electronics.

📦 BULK / BLOCK DEALS

Significant Buys

- Adani Energy Solutions (ADANIENSOL): PI Opportunities AIF V buys 49.5 lakh shares at ₹1,334, worth ~₹661 Cr, from Prazim Trading.

- Manipal Health Enterprises (MANIPALHOS): PI Opportunities AIF V buys 19 lakh shares at ₹630, worth ~₹120 Cr, from Prazim Trading.

- S P R Auto Technologies (SHRIPISTON): PI Opportunities AIF V buys 2.57 lakh shares at ₹4,490, worth ~₹115 Cr, from Prazim Trading.

- Aditya Birla Capital (ABCAPITAL): PI Opportunities AIF V buys 30.7 lakh shares at ₹366, worth ~₹112 Cr, from Prazim Trading.

- H D Fire Protect (HDFIRE): Allianz buys 17.6 lakh shares at ₹317.48, worth ~₹56 Cr.

- Craftsman Automation (CRAFTSMAN): PI Opportunities AIF V buys 28,735 shares at ₹10,975, worth ~₹32 Cr, from Prazim Trading.

- Jindal Supreme (JSIPL): Neomile buys 10.8 lakh shares at ₹149.94, worth ~₹16 Cr.

Significant Sells

- Amir Chand Jagdish Kumar (AEROPLANE): Shlok Vimal Rathod sells 5.85 lakh shares at ₹209.59, worth ~₹12 Cr.

👤 PROMOTER / INSIDER ACTIVITY

Promoter / Insider Buys

- Afcom Holdings: Promoter Manjula Annamalai acquires 10.5 lakh shares (3.7%) at ₹800 through an off-market transfer from promoter Jaganmohan Manthena. Inter-se transfer; promoter-group holding unchanged.

- Sindhu Trade Links: Promoters Rudra Sen Sindhu and Vir Sen Sindhu receive 3.5% through a gift. Inter-se transfer among relatives; promoter-group holding remains 73.9%.

- Koura Fine Diamond Jewellery: Promoters acquire 2.2 lakh shares (3.5%) through a preferential issue.

Pledge Updates

- Cineline India: Promoters release pledge on 65 lakh shares on October 19. Encumbered holding falls to 0%.

- Deepak Builders & Engineers India: 20 lakh shares (0.5%) pledged in favour of Comfort Fincap, a non-promoter entity.

RUSSIA-UKRAINE PEACE TALKS – PUTIN AGREES TO RESUME TRILATERAL NEGOTIATIONS
Geopolitical Update

Key Highlights
- Putin agreed in principle to resume Russia-US-Ukraine peace talks in November.
- Talks could begin around November 10 in Abu Dhabi.
- US envoy Steve Witkoff held nearly three-hour talks with Putin.
- Discussions focused on a potential framework to end the Ukraine war.
- Zelenskyy expressed support for holding trilateral negotiations in early November.
- US officials said technical-level discussions could resume soon.
- Putin and Witkoff also discussed potential joint economic projects.
- Kremlin says new European and Ukrainian proposals offer limited value.
- China is preparing for a possible Trump-Putin-Xi meeting at the November APEC summit.
- No final peace agreement has been announced.

Key Takeaway
- Renewed negotiations offer a potential diplomatic opening.
- A ceasefire and lasting peace remain uncertain.
- Energy markets, sanctions and global trade remain key monitorables.
- Impact: Potentially Positive for Global Risk Sentiment

#Q2FY27
**Rating: REDUCE**

- Q2FY27 revenue stood at US$1,235.2 Mn, up 1.1% QoQ.
- AI revenue grew 12.7% QoQ.
- AI contributed 13.4% of total revenue.
- Non-AI revenue declined 0.6% QoQ.
- EBIT margins remained broadly stable and in line with estimates.

**Deal Pipeline & Growth**
- Deal TCV declined 25% QoQ and 20.8% YoY.
- Shift towards shorter-tenure AI deals reduced reported TCV.
- Management targets approximately 6% organic USD revenue growth in FY27.
- ICICI Securities views achieving this target as challenging.
- Weak non-AI revenue remains a key concern.

**AI Strategy & Investments**
- Launched BlueVerse One Token and BlueVerse RightLogic.
- Expanded AI partnerships with Anthropic and IBM.
- AI engagements offer better gross-margin potential.
- Management aims to maintain FY27 organic EBIT margins near FY26 levels.

**Other Business Updates**
- H1 growth came mainly from outside the top five clients.
- Top-five client revenue has started returning to growth.
- Headcount increased by 949 to 88,835 employees.
- Added 1,743 freshers during the quarter.
- Operating cash flow declined due to gratuity provisions and advance tax payments.

**Valuation & Brokerage View**
- ICICI Securities maintains REDUCE with a ₹3,720 target.
- Current price: ₹4,235.
- Valuation stands at approximately 20x FY27E P/E.
- FY27E EPS estimated at ₹205.1.
- Brokerage cites stretched valuation and uncertain growth delivery.

**Key Takeaway**
- AI revenue is growing, but non-AI business remains weak.
- Lower deal TCV raises concerns over future revenue visibility.
- FY27 growth guidance appears challenging to achieve.
- Impact: **Negative**

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now

What regulators see that investors often ignore 👇

Every time a regulator acts, investors first ask: "How much EPS gets hit?" Regulators ask something else: "Is the market structure fair for the end consumer?" That's a very different lens. 
Thoughts on recent #PBFintech & older #IEX n more

Case in point: Recent change on insurance commissions. The proposed changes effectively aim to reduce distribution costs & curb excessive upfront payouts on some products. Investors see lower margins. Regulators see lower customer acquisition costs & better value for policyholders.

Truth is, hardly anyone argues that insurance has zero mis-selling. Higher upfront commissions have often created incentives to sell what pays the most, not what suits the customer best. If that problem exists, intervention shouldn't be surprising.

The irony is that many investors celebrate efficiency in every industry except their own portfolio holdings. When a regulator targets excess distribution costs, the reaction is often outrage instead of introspection.

Look at insurance expense ratios. Even as the industry scaled up, commission/expense pools as a % of premium remained elevated in several segments. The regulator's job is to ask: why isn't scale translating into lower customer costs?

Learning from MFs TER. Every TER cut was seen as fatal attack. Prediction was: growth will die, distributors will vanish, profit collapse. Instead industry adapted. Players became efficient, direct plans gained share, technology reduced costs, investor participation & AUM surged

Market coupling in power exch. Investors focus: which exchange lose market share. Regulators focus: consumers get better price discovery. Market coupling means bids/orders from all exch get pooled to discover a single price. One price improves efficiency & reduces fragmentation

Could one exchange lose moat? Maybe. But from system perspective, better price discovery, deeper liquidity & lower market distortion are hard to ignore.
Regulators rarely optimize for shareholder returns. They optimize for consumers, market efficiency & long-term public interest

Think about hospitals. If tomorrow there is stricter price regulation, hospital stocks may get hit. As investors we'd feel the pain. But can anyone honestly deny healthcare costs are becoming unaffordable for a large section of Indians?
One may argue India's healthcare is still cheaper than many countries. True. But the person comparing prices globally is not the same person struggling to pay a hospital bill locally.

Markets often assume regulators must protect industry profitability. Regulators believe industries shouldn't fleece poor customers. When public benefit & industry profits collide, the regulator's choice is usually obvious.

That's why stock market reaction is often the last variable in the regulator's decision. If a policy improves consumer outcomes, transparency, affordability or efficiency, temporary shareholder pain rarely changes the outcome.
